claims.text: Near-equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr initially forms either a single-phase BCC solid solution or BCC plus minor brittle intermetallics.
Conventional as-cast Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys typically have high strength.
Conventional as-cast Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys typically have less than 5% room-temperature ductility.
Near-equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr suffers from high density.
Rapid solidification will suppress equilibrium brittle-intermetallic formation in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
Rapid solidification will refine the grain structure of Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
Aging at 600–800 °C will nucleate metastable, coherent Ti-rich nanoscale precipitates without growing coarse brittle phases.
Ti-rich nanoprecipitates will impede dislocation motion and increase yield strength through precipitation hardening.
Metastable Ti-rich precipitates will improve room-temperature ductility by suppressing brittle phases and promoting localized shear banding.
A refined grain structure will provide Hall–Petch strengthening without sacrificing ductility.
Processing under an inert atmosphere is necessary to prevent oxidation.
The aging temperature must remain below the threshold for Laves- or sigma-phase formation.
The solidification cooling rate must exceed a critical value to retain high-temperature FCC or disordered BCC Ti-rich regions and avoid transformation to monoclinic brittle phases.
Rapid solidification suppresses the thermodynamic driving force for brittle-intermetallic formation.
The processed Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy will have room-temperature yield strength above 1000 MPa.
The processed Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy will have room-temperature tensile elongation above 10%.
The processed Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy will have density significantly below 8.0 g/cm³ and lower than Ni-based superalloys.
The precipitate-containing microstructure will remain stable during room-temperature deformation.
Large heats of formation may prevent high-entropy stabilization concepts from applying effectively to this alloy.
In NbMoTaWVTi, TiO precipitation and grain refinement increase strength while reducing ductility relative to the as-cast alloy.
